title: Projective nodal pinching along finite etale double branches
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C\to S$ be projective, flat and finitely presented with nonempty nodal geometric fibres [def-kun-projective, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $B\hookrightarrow C$ be a closed immersion into the relative smooth locus [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $B\to N$ be a finite etale morphism of constant degree two between finite etale $S$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. The empty case is allowed. The scheme pushout $Y=C\amalg_BN$ exists [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], is projective, flat and finitely presented over $S$, and has nodal geometric fibres. The map $C\to Y$ is finite and surjective, $N\to Y$ is a closed immersion, the square is also cartesian, and $C\setminus B\to Y\setminus N$ is an isomorphism. Formation of the square commutes with base change to the generic fibre and to geometric fibres. Compatible maps from $C$ and $N$ to any scheme induce a unique map from $Y$. For every open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion], the square of the inverse images of $V$ in $B$, $C$, $N$ and $V$ itself is again a pushout of schemes. A nodal geometric fibre here is reduced of pure dimension one, and each nonsmooth closed point has completed local ring $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The intermediate geometric fibres need not be connected.

source.place: Agent trait form of Tag 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral) and Tag 0E26 (lemma-pushout-separated). The split branch ring is the fibre product of two smooth branch rings over R. Projectivity uses descent of an ample line bundle after trivializing on the finite semilocal branch schemes. This is not the field-only pinching assertion.

proof.text: The finite degree-two map $B\to N$ is surjective: each fibre algebra has dimension two, hence is nonzero and its spectrum is nonempty [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Every ideal of a DVR is principal, hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; this is the base hypothesis of the two new nodes cited in steps 1 and 4. Its spectrum has only its generic and closed points, so the finite fibres of $B/S$ make $|B|$ finite [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-centre-proper-pinching] to $(X,Z,T)=(C,B,N)$. It supplies $Y,a,b$, an ample invertible $L$ on $C$, an affine $U\supset B$, properness of both $C/S$ and $Y/S$, finite presentation of $Y/S$, finiteness and surjectivity of $a$, the cartesian square, complement isomorphism, and its Ferrand affine charts.

The schemes $B,N$ are flat over $S$ because they are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $C/S$ is flat by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-trait-pinching-base-change] with $(X,Z,T,P)=(C,B,N,Y)$ and the affine $U$ from step 1. Its pushout hypothesis is supplied by that step, so this is the same $Y$ throughout. Thus $Y/S$ is flat and the square is a pushout after every affine scalar extension, in particular to $K$ and to every algebraically closed geometric-point field. Its tensor comparison uses flatness of the common quotient algebra of $B$, so includes the nonflat special-fibre extension.

source.place: Tag 0ET0 (lemma-basic-example-pushout) on affine charts of Tag 0E25; More on Algebra Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat); Algebra Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-nodal-pinching-criterion] to this $C,B,N,Y$: both $C/S$ and $Y/S$ are proper by step 1; $C/S$ is flat and finitely presented by hypothesis, $Y/S$ is finitely presented by step 1, and step 2 supplies the geometric-fibre pushouts. All hypotheses concerning $C$ and its smooth branches are the hypotheses of the item. It follows that the geometric fibres of $Y$ are nonempty, reduced of pure dimension one with precisely the stated nodal completions. This requires no connectedness or splitting over $R$.

The cartesian square identifies $B=a^{-1}N$, and the complement map is an isomorphism. Both schemes are proper over the Noetherian ring $R$ by step 1, which also gives the finite surjective $a$ and closed immersion $N\hookrightarrow Y$. With its $L,U$ and finite $|B|$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-branch-ample-descent] to $(X,Y,Z,T)=(C,Y,B,N)$. This gives an ample invertible $M$ on $Y$ with $a^*M\simeq L$ and a closed immersion of $Y$ into a finite projective space over $S$. Hence $Y/S$ is projective in exactly the convention of the item.

Finally [lem-sfb-finite-centre-proper-pinching] gives the pushout in all schemes and every open-restriction pushout. The former is exactly the unique factorization of compatible maps to an arbitrary scheme. If $B=N=\varnothing$, its affine formula reads $A\times_0 0=A$, so $Y=C$; all four applications include this case.
